# Solitito — guitar chord and note recognition

Recognition models for [**Solitito**](https://github.com/greblus/solitito), a
real-time guitar trainer written in Rust. Code, the trainer and documentation
are in the GitHub repository; this repository holds the binary artifacts the
app needs.

<div align="center">
<img width="640" alt="Solitito, Chords mode: shell voicings, one column per root string" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greblus/solitito/solitito-ai/docs/screenshots/en/solitito_chords.png" />
</div>

| file | |
|---|---|
| `best_model_v2_take6_chords.onnx` | the recognition model: what is sounding, the root and the chord quality, 29 MB |
| `short_onset_masking_v2.onnx` | the strike model: which pitch class was just **struck**, 1 MB |
| `dsp_weights.json` | pseudo-CQT kernel in sparse format, 2 MB |

## The recognition model

Takes 48 frames of features (144 CQT bins + 12 chroma + 12 bass energy, 16 kHz,
256-sample hop — 0.77 s of audio) and returns three outputs:

| output | shape | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `root_logits` | 13 | 12 pitch classes + "Noise" |
| `quality_logits` | 11 | maj, min, maj7, dom7, min7, m7b5, dim7, aug, sus, note, N |
| `pitch_logits` | 12 | sigmoid — which pitch classes are sounding |

"Sounding" includes a string ringing on, one resonating in sympathy, and the
note before — all of them true and none of them played just now. What was
actually struck is the strike model's question, below.

CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks, then a Transformer encoder with a CLS
token. 7.3M parameters, CPU inference.

### Results

Measured on a validation split grouped by source recording, with solo tracks
excluded:

| metric | |
|---|---|
| root accuracy | 98.1% |
| pitch F1 | 0.909 |
| exact match (root **and** quality) | 92.4% |

## The strike model

The recognition model sees 0.77 s at a time and is asked every 40 ms; that is
too coarse to tell whether a note that is already ringing was just struck
again. The strike model answers only that question, on every 16 ms hop:

| | |
|---|---|
| input `short_features` | `[batch, 770, time]` — two Hann windows of the newest audio (1024 and 2048 samples at 16 kHz), magnitudes up to 4 kHz, `ln(1 + 1000·a) / ln(1001)` |
| output `onset_logits` | `[batch, 12, time]` — sigmoid per pitch class: struck at this frame |
| context | causal; 34 past frames plus the current one (0.56 s) |
| metadata | `onset_threshold` = 0.9, `onset_history_frames` = 34 |

A projection of the spectra and of their rise against the previous four
frames, then four residual causal convolutions (dilations 1, 2, 4, 8).
260 thousand parameters; 0.7 ms per hop on a CPU.

It was trained as a branch beside the frozen recognition network and is cut out
of that combined file, so it does not run the chord network on every hop. The
branch never reads the chord input: its answer is identical to the last digit
whatever the other input is.

The app uses it for everything that depends on what was **struck** rather than
what is sounding: "Credit only what was struck" in the note modes (a class may be
credited only if the model reported it struck in the last 0.35 s), a chord asked
for twice in a row (it needs a fresh strike), and **repeats** — a note credited
once counts again only when that pitch class has been struck since, not when it
is merely still sounding. The app evens out the input level before the model and
ignores a second firing of the same class within 0.6 s. Measured on every reviewed note
of a labelled recording, spliced into new signals (the note alone, ringing out,
and struck again with the pick stopping the old vibration):

| | without the strike model | with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a repeat allowed while the note only rings | 24 / 51 | **0** / 51 |
| struck again after 0.8 s, counted in time | 36 / 51, 11 early | **48** / 51, none early |
| struck again after 1.2 s, counted in time | 35 / 51, 14 early | **50** / 51, none early |
| a note ringing into the next chord, credited there | 47 / 51 | **0** / 51 |

### Training data

GuitarSet whole takes (solo and comp, players split whole: 00–03 train, 04
validation, 05 test), Karplus–Strong synthetic plucks with exact attack times
(holds, re-plucks of a ringing note, octaves, an added third or fifth, re-struck
triads), and masking pairs: a quieter upper note struck over two ringing ones
at −18, −12, −6 or 0 dB, each with its background alone and itself alone.
Levels vary by ±6 dB in training.

## Training

Each model has its own trainer in `dist/` of the GitHub repository, one file to
paste into a Kaggle GPU notebook: `model_trainer.py` for the recognition model
(it writes `best_model_v2_take6_chords.onnx`), `strike_trainer.py` for
the strike model, whose defaults are the recipe of `short_onset_masking_v2.onnx`.
See `docs/training.md` there.

## Using it

Put the files next to the Solitito binary; the release packages already
contain them. `SOLITITO_MODEL` points the app at another recognition model
file. The strike model is optional: without it the app still
starts and judges repeats on a pitch-blind attack detector. `./solitito --check` verifies
what is there and prints the strike model's threshold.

Feeding these models your own features requires matching the DSP exactly — the
input is not raw audio. For the recognition model, `dist/gen_weights.py` in the
GitHub repository produces the kernel, and `dsp_weights.json` here is its output.
For the strike model, `src/strike.rs` (`ShortFeatures`) and the trainer compute
the same features, and a shared test fixture holds them to the same numbers.

## Training data of the recognition model

Two sources: a synthetic set rendered through [NAM](https://www.neuralampmodeler.com/)
amp models with exact labels, and [GuitarSet](https://guitarset.weebly.com/) for
real playing.

Getting GuitarSet right took four runs. Half of it is `_solo` — monophonic
improvisation carrying the accompaniment's chord annotation — and its
`instructed` chord labels contain no `maj7` or `min7` at all, while calling 500
segments `m` that were played as `m7`. Fixing those two moved exact match from
44.8% to 92.4%. The details, with numbers, are in the GitHub README.
